scope: Eight native-backend CGU16 controls comparing the final code candidate with the original baseline. This file does not include ETT or workspace-test results.
conclusion: Dense member consumption improves substantially; staged chain and fan-in are near baseline in this CGU16 run. Sparse incremental and equality closure remain slower.
source_manifest_encoding: SHA256 of sorted UTF-8 records: relative_path + NUL + lowercase_file_sha256 + newline. Source snapshots were byte-checked against git archive for their exact revision.

generation.validation: Frozen generated bench_model.eql.rs hashes match outputs previously regenerated with exact-source f29 and 7643 compilers. The eqlog compiler tree, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are unchanged between 7643e68 and final 8792fa1. Flat generated source is identical in both variants.

methodology.isolation: All builds used a shared activity lock; each entire adjacent case group held the exclusive activity lock. Timing began after the final ETT build released that lock. No profiler or allocator instrumentation was enabled.

interleaved_control.purpose: An intermediate comparison was measured in the same balanced batch; its results and binaries are omitted from this final-vs-baseline report.

methodology.aggregation: Within each process, sort retained sample durations and take the middle value. Report the median of the two process medians (their arithmetic midpoint), then divide candidate by baseline.
methodology.setup_validation_teardown: Fresh fixture per sample. Fixture setup, post-timing validation, and destruction are excluded. Warm pair additionally performs one untimed full scan before its measured scan.
methodology.limitations: Two process medians are a small sample; no confidence interval or significance claim is made. Results describe these workloads and this toolchain/CPU. Code-generation settings affect performance, so these CGU16 numbers should not be substituted for CGU1 or ETT results.

workload_definitions.pair_warm_consume: Two worlds with 256 members each; source has all 256^2 pair rows and a full index-preserving morphism. Close and consume once before timing; time one complete ordered scan of both worlds (131072 rows).
workload_definitions.mixed_close_consume: Two worlds with 256 members each and three global labels; source has all 3*256^2 mixed rows. Insert a full index-preserving morphism, then time closure plus complete ordered consumption of both worlds (393216 rows).
workload_definitions.flat_common: 2048 items. Sparse left edges i->i+1 and i->i+17; right edges i->i and i->i+31, modulo n. Rules derive joined(x,z) from left(x,y), right(y,z), and select joined rows whose first item is asked. Only model.close() is timed.
workload_definitions.sparse_initial: Time initial closure of the flat fixture with every eighth item already asked.
workload_definitions.sparse_query: Close the flat fixture without requests, add requests for every eighth item, then time closure.
workload_definitions.sparse_incremental: Initially omit the last item left edges, close, add its two missing left edges, then time closure.
workload_definitions.sparse_equality: Close the full flat fixture, equate items 0 and 1, then time equality propagation and closure.
workload_definitions.lifecycle_common: 128 members per world and three labels. Insert sparse facts and identity member images in 16 batches, calling close after every batch. Each source contributes mixed(index,label,(index+1+7*world+3*label)%n). Apply equalities in source, middle and sink worlds at zero-based batches 4, 9, 13. Time all mutations/closures and one final full scan; intermediate results remain unconsumed. No quotient-map or query variant is used.
workload_definitions.chain_delayed: 17 worlds linked by 16 successive morphisms; fact sources are worlds 0 and 8.
workload_definitions.fanin_delayed: Eight source worlds map to world 8, which maps to sink world 9.

validation.consumer: Every sample checks exact row count and an order-sensitive rolling checksum independently constructed from all expected tuples.
validation.flat: Every sample compares full joined and selected BTreeSets against an independent canonical relational join, then checks counts/checksum across variants. This harness does not separately reject duplicate iterator rows before set collection.
validation.lifecycle: Every sample checks the full final canonical row set, equality partition, images, memberships and query results against an independent fixed-point relational oracle; duplicate/noncanonical public rows are rejected. The timed scan count/checksum must match that oracle.
validation.cross_variant: Semantic fingerprint fields recorded per workload match for all baseline, candidate and interleaved-control processes. All warmup samples also execute validation.
